standard.title: Create arts works that communicate ideas
standard.description: create arts works that communicate ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have experience with play and exploration of materials, voice, movement and digital devices in early childhood settings. They can express ideas through drawing, movement and role play but have not yet deliberately used media technologies to communicate ideas to an audience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create arts works using available materials, technologies or tools that communicate a recognisable idea from personal or social experience.

nodes.label: Idea to arts form
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a personal or social idea and choose a form (image, sound, movement, story) to communicate it.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one personal idea and identify one form that could be used to communicate it.
nodes.typical_width: Explore multiple forms (captured images, voice recording, movement, puppet play) and explain how each could communicate the same idea differently.
wider: Use digital devices (tablet, camera) to explore how the same idea looks different when captured versus drawn versus acted out
Respond to literature or artworks from own cultural community as a starting point — identifying what idea they want to communicate and why
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot connect a personal idea to a media form, subsequent making decisions are arbitrary — they cannot make intentional choices about materials, sequencing or communication.

response_modes.reason: Expose students to multiple forms early — seeing their own idea communicated across image, sound and movement helps them understand that form is a choice, not a default.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The variety of forms available at Foundation (digital capture, voice, objects, movement) is genuinely rich — students who explore multiple forms develop a stronger intuition for what media arts is and what communicative choices mean.
success_criteria: Student can name an idea from their own life or experience they want to communicate
Student can identify at least one form (captured image, voice recording, or object play) that could communicate that idea

nodes.label: Making and constructing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use available materials or technologies to make an arts work that embodies their idea.
nodes.minimum_width: Create one arts work (e.g. a sequence of captured images, a voice-over recording, a puppet retelling) using at least one available material or technology.
nodes.typical_width: Create arts works across two or more forms or materials — combining images, sounds, objects or digital tools to communicate ideas; manipulate choices (which images to keep, how to sequence events, which sounds to add).
wider: Repurpose everyday materials (boxes, clothing) as environments or characters, and document the creation using a digital device
Devise and record a chant or rap on a digital device that communicates a message or retells a story — sharing via a school-managed platform
Explore claymation or stop-motion animation by manipulating objects and capturing a sequence of images

response_modes.reason: The making process at Foundation integrates idea, material and tool — support students in connecting their intended communication with the choices they make during construction rather than treating making as separate from meaning.
Vary the making modalities — digital capture, voice, object manipulation, repurposed materials — so students who are ready encounter the full diversity of making contexts available at Foundation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of making modalities available at Foundation (digital capture, voice, object manipulation, repurposed materials) is genuinely diverse — students who explore across modalities build a richer understanding of what 'making' means in media arts.
success_criteria: Student creates an arts work using at least one material or technology
Student can describe what their work communicates or what it is about

nodes.label: Communicating to an audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can present or share their arts work and explain what idea it communicates.
nodes.minimum_width: Share one arts work with a teacher or small group and respond to 'What is your work about?' with a recognisable connection to their original idea.
nodes.typical_width: Share arts works with peers and teacher; describe the idea communicated and what was enjoyable about making it; extend or vary a familiar form (changing words, adding actions) to communicate a new idea.
wider: Share a work created from a health, sustainability or process message — presenting it live or via a school-managed space and explaining why the message matters
Use questions about the story ('What happens next?', 'What else could happen?') to extend and develop the work for a second audience

response_modes.reason: Sharing and communicating closes the making loop — students connect their original idea to what the audience perceives. This is the integration moment: idea → making → audience response.

success_criteria: Student shares their arts work with at least one other person
Student can articulate what idea their work communicates when asked
